current_activity: army command post near Lisieux; Model confers with Dietrich, Eberbach and Hausser
notes: Event date: early on 18 August, at 0600, Model drove to the Fifth Panzer Army command post near Lisieux to confer with Dietrich, Eberbach and Hausser (Breakout and Pursuit ch. 27 p. 532). Location approximate: the source says 'near Lisieux'; the point is Lisieux (10 km). Commander: Dietrich commanded the army from the second Avranches attack planning (ch. 25 p. 483), after Eberbach took over Panzer Group Eberbach.

commander: General der Panzertruppen Hasso von Manteuffel
current_activity: Manteuffel asks to withdraw the Fifth Panzer Army; Balck refuses at midnight and orders the link-up with the 553rd
notes: Event date: CMH Lorraine Campaign ch. 5 p. 235: "asked for permission to withdraw the entire Fifth Panzer Army" ... "at midnight General Balck refused". Event definition: the refusal on the night of 22-23 September; the row date is 22 September, the day of the request. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: the army front lay between Château-Salins and Lunéville around Arracourt (the point of PL0015), with a precision of 25 km. Location approximate: a representative point for the army sector. Location support: CMH describes the LVIII and XLVII Panzer Corps fronts either side of the Marne-Rhine canal near Arracourt; no army headquarters place is given. Commander: General der Panzertruppen Hasso von Manteuffel. Opponents: US XII Corps (4th Armored Division).

commander: General der Panzertruppen Hasso von Manteuffel
current_activity: The 11th Panzer Division takes Marsal and Moyenvic and meets the First Army at Vic-sur-Seille
notes: Event date: CMH Lorraine Campaign ch. 5 p. 238: "the Germans seized Marsal" and "One prong of the German drive continued through Moyenvic and by noon had come to a halt at Vic-sur-Seille--finally effecting the junction with the First Army which Berlin had decreed". Event definition: the attack of 25 September, which jumped off at 0900. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Vic-sur-Seille, where the junction took place, with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point of the northern thrust, not the army headquarters. Location support: CMH names the town. Commander: General der Panzertruppen Hasso von Manteuffel. Opponents: US 4th Armored Division CCA, 25th Cavalry Squadron.
